title: Hot Inflation Shocks Markets: The Worst Is Still To Come | Steve Hanke
speaker: Steve Hanke

macro_themes.theme: Inflation genie out of the bottle
macro_themes.view: Broad money (Divisia M4) growing ~7.5%, above the ~6% consistent with 2%, so all inflation measures stay above target until money growth slows.
Physical oil trades 35-40% above futures, backwardation reflects abnormally low inventories, and the diesel squeeze lasts into 2027 per IEA, which he agrees with.
Rising money supply and velocity argue against a recession anytime soon, though real wages are falling.
Interest rates stay high until money supply growth slows, which is not happening; AI capex credit demand is fueling it.
Defers to CME odds (67% no hike) and expects no change in fed funds at the next meeting.

calls.reason: Post-Hormuz logistics bottlenecks, tanker shortage and abnormally low inventories keep physical oil and diesel prices elevated; backwardation signals storage shortage, not lower prices ahead.
calls.quote: they have the right diagnosis that these prices will sur stay high for quite some time.

calls.condition: Rates stay high until money supply growth slows
calls.reason: Money supply keeps growing on AI-driven credit demand, so yields stay elevated rather than falling.
calls.quote: Well, they'll stay high until the money supply starts slowing down.

notes: TNX view is 'stays high' (no direction beyond staying elevated), recorded as neutral medium-term. Oil price quoted is Brent spot ~108 (host's figure), normalized to CL. Gold mentioned only as a hypothetical store of value in double-digit inflation; skipped.
